rows.notes: The cited work is a global meta-analysis of 74 published papers (Section 2.1) on deficit irrigation effects on seed cotton yield and water productivity; it reports no primary data, so Q1 is 'no'. The soil-texture explanation in the passage (fine soils with poor aeration, coarse soils with poor water/nutrient holding) appears only in the Discussion (Section 4.4) as an interpretation of pooled results and is attributed to other authors (Bollmann and Conrad, Tiedje, Du et al., Lu et al.). The meta-analysis compares deficit versus full irrigation, not surface versus subsurface drip, and found no significant soil-texture effect (Fig. 6).

Meta-analysis, not a primary study (Q1 'no'). The claim that drip wets a small part of the soil, improving aeration and uptake of water and nutrients and thereby yield, appears in Section 4.2 as a speculative explanation citing Bonachela et al. (2001) and Kang et al. (2004); soil aeration was not measured. The pooled result it relates to is that under deficit irrigation the yield decrease with drip (-19.5%) was similar to furrow (-19.6%) and smaller than sprinkler (-36.2%) (Fig. 3a), with no significant WP difference among methods (Fig. 3b).
